reason: The muscle-development messengers are shown meeting receivers on the unspecialized cells and activating muscle genes. That seems like a first step toward copying their instructions.
expectation: The messengers will direct a group of cells toward the muscle pathway.

alternatives.reason: The support-cell pathway is also a goal, but I can start with muscle.

effect: The muscle messengers produced cells with muscle-protein RNA, and the next goal is to make their pulling proteins.
reaction: The picture makes it clear that the RNA is a copy and the protein still needs to be made.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and these cells now have the RNA instructions for muscle proteins.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to build pulling proteins.

alternatives.reason: I could start the other RNA goal first, but I want to follow the muscle pathway.

effect: The amino acids made muscle cells with protein fibres that can slide to shorten the cells. The support-protein pathway is still unfinished.
reaction: Seeing the instructions lead to fibres that can shorten the cell was satisfying.
reason: The supporting-cell messengers are shown activating support-protein genes in another group of the population.
expectation: The messengers will produce cells with RNA copies of support-protein instructions.

effect: The supporting-cell messengers produced cells with support-protein RNA, and the remaining goal is to build fibres around them.
reaction: The picture clearly separates the RNA instructions from the fibres that have yet to be made.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and these cells now have instructions for support proteins, just as the muscle cells had instructions for pulling proteins.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids to build supporting fibres around themselves.

effect: The amino acids helped the cells build supporting connective tissue around themselves, completing the chapter. This contrasts with the muscle cells keeping their pulling proteins inside.
reaction: The contrast between proteins inside cells and fibres around cells made the two paths clearer.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building muscle cells from the RNA instructions was most worthwhile: the picture connected the instructions to fibres that can shorten a cell.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second pathway felt somewhat repetitive because it followed the same messenger-then-amino-acids pattern, although the different result was useful.

surprise.text: The support cells released protein to build material around themselves, rather than keeping the fibres inside like the muscle cells.

arbitrary.text: None of the pairings felt especially arbitrary: the pictures and goals explained the messengers, RNA and protein building blocks well enough to follow them.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how these different cells become larger tissues and organs, though I hope the next chapter offers a less repetitive pattern.
